text: If y = y(x) is the solution curve of the differential equation $x^{2}dy+\left (y-\frac{1}{x}\right )dx=0$ ; x > 0 and y(1) = 1, then $y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2}dy+\left (y-\frac{1}{x}\right )dx=0$ ; x > 0, y(1) = 1

$x^{2}dy+\frac{(xy-1)}{x}dx=0$

$x^{2}dy=\frac{(xy-1)}{x}dx$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1-xy}{x^{3}}$

$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{x^{3}}-\frac{y}{x^{2}}$

$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}.y=\frac{1}{x^{3}}$

I.F. = $e^{\int \frac{1}{x2}dx}=e^{-\frac{1}{x}}$

$ye^{-\frac{1}{x}}=\int \frac{1}{x^{3}}.e^{-\frac{1}{x}}$

$ye^{-\frac{1}{x}}=e^{-\frac{1}{x}}\left (1+\frac{1}{x}\right )+C$

$1.e^{-1}=e^{-1}(2)+C$

$C=-e^{-1}=-\frac{1}{e}$

$ye^{-\frac{1}{x}}=e^{-\frac{1}{x}}\left (1+\frac{1}{x}\right )-\frac{1}{e}$

$y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=3-\frac{1}{e}\times e^{2}$

$y\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )=3-e$

text: The number of pairs (a, b) of real numbers, such that whenever $α$ is a root of the equation $x^{2} + ax + b = 0$, $α^{2}$ $-$ 2 is also a root of this equation, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Consider the equation $x^{2} + ax + b = 0$

It has two roots (not necessarily real $α$ & $β$)

Either $α$ = $β$ or $α$ $\neq$ $β$

Case (1) If $α$ = $β$, then it is repeated root. Given that $α^{2}$ $-$ 2 is also a root

So, $α$ = $α^{2}$ $-$ 2 $\Rightarrow$ ($α$ + 1)($α$ $-$ 2) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = $-$1 or $α$ = 2

When $α$ = $-$1 then (a, b) = (2, 1)

$α$ = 2 then (a, b) = ($-$4, 4)

Case (2) If $α$ $\neq$ $β$

Then

(I) $α$ = $α^{2}$ $-$ 2 and $β$ = $β^{2}$ $-$ 2

Hence, (a, b) = ($-$($α$ + $β$), $αβ$)

($-$1, $-$2)

(II) $α$ = $β^{2}$ $-$ 2 and $β$ = $α^{2}$ $-$ 2

Then $α$ $-$ $β$ = $β^{2}$ $-$ $α^{2}$ = ($β$ $-$ $α$) ($β$ + $α$)

Since $α$ $\neq$ $β$ we get $α$ + $β$ = $β^{2}$ + $α^{2}$ $-$ 4

$α$ + $β$ = ($α$ + $β)^{2}$ $-$ 2$αβ$ $-$ 4

Thus $-$1 = 1 $-$2 $αβ$ $-$ 4 which implies

$αβ$ = $-$1 Therefore (a, b) = ($-$($α$ + $β$), $αβ$)

= (1, $-$1)

(III) $α$ = $α^{2}$ $-$ 2 = $β^{2}$ $-$ 2 and $α$ $\neq$ $β$

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = $-$ $β$

Thus $α$ = 2, $β$ = $-$2

$α$ = $-$1, $β$ = 1

Therefore (a, b) = (0, $-$4) & (0, $-$1)

(IV) $β$ = $α^{2}$ $-$ 2 = $β^{2}$ $-$ 2 and $α$ $\neq$ $β$ is same as (III) Therefore we get 6 pairs of (a, b)

Which are (2, 1), ($-$4, 4), ($-$1, $-$2), (1, $-$1), (0, $-$4), (0, $-$1)

Option (a)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: Let $P_{1}, P_{2}, ......, P_{15}$ be 15 points on a circle. The number of distinct triangles formed by points $P_{i}, P_{j}, P_{k}$ such that i +j + k $\neq$ 15, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The 15 points lie on a circle, so no three are collinear and the total number of triangles is ${}^{15}C_{3}=455$.

Triangles with $i+j+k=15$ correspond to sets of distinct indices $i<j<k$ with sum 15:

With $i=1$: $\{1,2,12\},\{1,3,11\},\{1,4,10\},\{1,5,9\},\{1,6,8\}$, that is 5 sets.

With $i=2$: $\{2,3,10\},\{2,4,9\},\{2,5,8\},\{2,6,7\}$, that is 4 sets.

With $i=3$: $\{3,4,8\},\{3,5,7\}$, that is 2 sets.

With $i=4$: $\{4,5,6\}$, that is 1 set.

No set has $i\geq 5$, since then $i+j+k\geq 5+6+7=18$. So $5+4+2+1=12$ triangles have $i+j+k=15$.

Required number $=455-12=443$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text:
Let f(x) be a polynomial of degree 3 such that
 $f(k)=-\frac{2}{k}$ for k = 2, 3, 4, 5. Then the value of 52 $-$ 10f(10) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $g(x)=xf(x)+2$. Since $f$ has degree 3, $g$ is a polynomial of degree 4.

For $k=2,3,4,5$: $g(k)=k\left (-\dfrac{2}{k}\right )+2=0$, so $2,3,4,5$ are the four roots of $g$:

$xf(x)+2=λ(x-2)(x-3)(x-4)(x-5)$

At $x=0$: $2=λ(-2)(-3)(-4)(-5)=120λ\Rightarrow λ=\dfrac{1}{60}$.

At $x=10$: $10f(10)+2=\dfrac{1}{60}(8)(7)(6)(5)=28\Rightarrow 10f(10)=26$.

$52-10f(10)=52-26=26$

Hence, the answer is 26.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: All the arrangements, with or without meaning, of the word FARMER are written excluding any word that has two R appearing together. The arrangements are listed serially in the alphabetic order as in the English dictionary. Then the serial number of the word FARMER in this list is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The letters of FARMER in alphabetical order are A, E, F, M, R, R, and a word is left out when its two R's are adjacent.

Words beginning with A: the letters E, F, M, R, R give $\dfrac{5!}{2!}=60$ arrangements, of which $4!=24$ have the two R's together (RR taken as one block). This leaves $60-24=36$.

Words beginning with E: in the same way, $36$.

Words beginning with FAE: M, R, R can follow as MRR, RMR or RRM; only RMR keeps the R's apart, so $1$ word (FAERMR).

Words beginning with FAM: E, R, R can follow as ERR, RER or RRE; only RER is allowed, so $1$ word (FAMRER).

Words beginning with FARE: M and R follow in $2!=2$ ways (FAREMR, FARERM), neither with the R's together.

Words beginning with FARM: E, R follow as ER or RE, and the first of these is FARMER itself.

$\text{Serial number}=36+36+1+1+2+1=77$

Hence, the answer is 77.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: Let $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$. Let a vector $\vec{v}$ be in the plane containing $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. If $\vec{v}$ is perpendicular to the vector $3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$ and its projection on $\vec{a}$ is 19 units, then $\left |2\vec{v}\right |^{2}$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$

$\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$

$\vec{c}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}$

$\vec{v}=x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}$

$\vec{v}\left (3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )=0$

$\vec{v}.\widehat{a}=19$

$\vec{v}=λ\vec{c}\times \left (\vec{a}\times \vec{b}\right )$

$\vec{v}=λ\left [\left (\vec{c}.\vec{b}\right )\vec{a}-\left (\vec{c}.\vec{a}\right )\vec{b}\right ]$

$=λ[(3+4+1)\left (2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}\right )-(6-2-2)\left (\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\widehat{k}\right )$

$=λ[16\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+16\widehat{k}-2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}]$

$\vec{v}=λ\left [14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\widehat{k}\right ]$

$λ[14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\widehat{k}].\frac{\left (2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}\right )}{\sqrt{4+1+4}}=19$

$λ\frac{[28+12+36]}{3}=19$

$λ\left (\frac{76}{3}\right )=19$

$4λ=3\Rightarrow λ=\frac{3}{4}$

$\left |2\vec{v}\right |^{2}=\left |2\times \frac{3}{4}(14\hat{i}-12\hat{j}+18\widehat{k})\right |^{2}$

$\frac{9}{4}\times 4\left (7\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+9\widehat{k}\right )^{2}$

$=9(49+36+81)$

$=9(166)$

$=1494$

text: Let [t] denote the greatest integer $\leq$ t. The number of points where the function $f(x)=[x]\left |x^{2}-1\right |+\sin \left (\frac{π}{[x]+3}\right )-[x+1],x\in (-2,2)$ is not continuous is $_____________$.

solution.body:
$f(x)=[x]\left |x^{2}-1\right |+\sin \left (\frac{π}{[x]+3}\right )-[x+1]$

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} -2\left |x^{2}-1\right |+1, & -2<x<-1 \\ -\left |x^{2}-1\right |+1, & -1\leq x<0 \\ \sin \frac{π}{3}-1, & 0\leq x<1 \\ \left |x^{2}-1\right |+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-2, & 1\leq x<2 \end{array} \right.$

$\therefore$ at x = -1, $\lim _{x\to -1^{-}}f(x)=1$ and $\lim _{x\to -1^{+}}f(x)=1$

Hence continuous at x = –1

Similarly check at x = 0,

$\lim _{x\to 0^{-}}f(x)=0$ and $\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-1$

So, f(x) discontinuous
and at x = 0

$\lim _{x\to 1^{-}}f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-1$ and $\lim _{x\to 1^{+}}f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-2$

So, f(x) discontinuous
and at x = 1

Hence 2 points of discontinuity.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift

text: A man starts walking from the point P($-$3, 4), touches the x-axis at R, and then turns to reach at the point Q(0, 2). The man is walking at a constant speed. If the man reaches the point Q in the minimum time, then $50\left ((PR)^{2}+(RQ)^{2}\right )$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 1st September Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


For minimum $(PR+RQ)$

$R$ lies on $PQ^{'}$ (where $Q^{'}$ is image of $Q$ in $X$-axis)

$\Rightarrow$ Equation of $PQ^{'}$ is

$2x+y+2=0\Rightarrow R(-1,0)$

$\therefore$ $50(PR^{2} + RQ^{2})$

= 50(20 + 5)

= 50(25)

= 1250
